source: mastery-advantage/english/gse-knowledge-space.json: young-learner reading and listening objectives, GSE 22–29 (A1 band, Quest books). Short ids: skill letter, GSE, and the order inside that GSE value in the graph (the A0 key rule). Track level_banks_20261002, 2026-10-02.

objectives.text: Can recognise some familiar words related to themselves and their family (e.g. ‘girl’, ‘brother’).
Can recognise ordinal numbers up to 20 written as words.
Can understand simple contractions (e.g. ‘I’m’, ‘he’s’, ‘we’re’).
Can read sentences correctly from left to right.
Can understand basic written instructions for classroom activities (e.g. ‘Read and match’).
Can identify familiar words in short, simple texts.
Can recognise cardinal numbers up to 100 written as words.
Can understand the relationship between words from the same vocabulary set (e.g. ‘colours’, ‘foods’, ‘classroom objects’).
Can understand short, simple descriptions of familiar places, if supported by pictures.
Can guess the meaning of a word from an accompanying picture.
Can recognise simple words and phrases related to familiar topics if supported by pictures.
Can use knowledge of alphabetical order to find words in a dictionary.
Can understand basic sentences naming familiar everyday items, if supported by pictures.
Can understand simple sentences, given prompts.
Can recognise key words and basic phrases in short, simple cartoon stories.
Can find proper names (e.g. ‘people’, ‘places’, ‘nationalities’) in short, simple texts by looking for capital letters.
Can understand basic phrases in short, simple texts.
Can recognise words or phrases that are repeated in a short text or poem.
Can understand a simple text if supported by pictures.
Can understand a few simple phrases related to familiar, everyday activities.
Can distinguish between a negative statement and a positive statement.
Can understand simple sentences about the weather, if supported by pictures.
Can identify individual sounds within simple words.
Can identify repeated words or phrases in a short text.
Can understand basic sentences describing someone’s physical appearance, (e.g. ‘eye/hair colour’, ‘height’), if supported by pictures.
Can understand basic sentences about things people have, if supported by pictures.
Can link letters and sounds when reading words.
Can follow simple dialogues in short illustrated stories, if they can listen while reading.
Can understand basic information about people’s likes and dislikes, if supported by pictures.
Can follow short, simple written directions (e.g. ‘go from X to Y’).
Can guess what a story or text is about from the pictures.
Can understand short, simple descriptions of objects, people and animals if supported by pictures.
Can understand the information in a simple school timetable giving days and times of classes.
Can understand basic sentences describing familiar everyday items (e.g. ‘colour’, ‘size’), if supported by pictures.
Can understand simple informational material containing familiar words, if supported by pictures (e.g. ‘a menu with pictures of food’).
Can understand basic sentences about where things, animals or people are.
Can recognise familiar words on product labels.
Can get the gist of a very simple illustrated story.
Can read the time when written as words.
Can follow basic instructions for making something (e.g. ‘a mask’, ‘a clock’), if supported by pictures.
Can combine a range of letter sounds to read some common words (e.g. ‘sing’, ‘high’).
Can guess what happens next in a story from the pictures.
Can infer basic information about a character’s preferences from pictures.
Can understand short, simple messages about when and where to meet.
Can understand short, simple illustrated narratives about everyday activities.
Can recognise ordinal numbers up to 50 written as words.
Can translate simple words and phrases with the help of a bilingual dictionary.
Can understand basic key words in short notes or messages.
Can understand basic questions about what things are in their immediate surroundings or in pictures (e.g. ‘What’s this?’).
Can recognise basic time words (e.g. ‘days’, ‘months’) in simple phrases or sentences.
Can distinguish between ‘can’ and ‘can’t’.
Can understand the time of day when expressed to the quarter hour.
Can understand simple phrases about likes and dislikes.
Can understand short, simple questions related to basic personal information, if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can understand simple feedback from a teacher.
Can understand simple contractions (e.g. ‘I’m’, ‘he’s’, ‘we’re’).
Can understand the time of day when expressed to within five minutes.
Can recognise familiar key words and phrases in short, basic descriptions (e.g. of ‘objects’, ‘people’ or ‘animals’), if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can recognise familiar words and basic phrases in short illustrated stories, if read out slowly and clearly.
Can understand basic phrases or sentences about things people have if supported by pictures.
Can understand basic statements about where things or people are, if spoken slowly and clearly and supported by pictures or gestures.
Can understand basic phrases about the weather, if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can recognise ordinal numbers up to 50, if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can understand basic questions about personal details if spoken slowly and clearly and supported by pictures.
Can understand simple directions, if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can recognise words and simple phrases related to familiar topics, if spoken slowly and clearly and supported by pictures.
Can get the gist of short, simple stories, if told slowly and clearly and supported by pictures or gestures.
Can understand the time of day when expressed to the half hour.
Can understand basic expressions or questions related to immediate personal needs, if delivered slowly and clearly.
Can identify the day and date in short, simple dialogues, if spoken slowly and clearly and supported by pictures or gestures.
Can understand basic information about someone’s immediate family, if spoken slowly and clearly and supported by pictures or gestures.
Can understand simple language related to naming and describing people’s clothes.
Can identify a caller’s name and phone number from a short, simple telephone conversation.
Can understand straightforward instructions, if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can recognise words or phrases that are repeated in a short dialogue or poem.
Can understand simple phrases related to familiar topics, if spoken slowly and clearly and supported by pictures.
Can understand simple questions and answers about peoples likes and dislikes.
Can identify the names of people or places in short, simple dialogues, if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can identify people in their immediate surroundings or in pictures from a short, simple description of their physical appearance and clothes.
Can recognise key information (e.g. ‘place’, ‘time’) about everyday events, if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can identify common objects from descriptions, if spoken slowly and clearly.
Can understand simple sentences on familiar topics if spoken slowly and clearly and with pauses.
Can understand what people say they can or can’t do from simple sentences spoken slowly and clearly.
Can follow a short, familiar traditional story, if supported by gestures and repetition.
Can understand basic information in short passages about everyday activities or routines, if spoken slowly and clearly and supported by prompts.
Can understand basic information about prices, times, and dates in familiar contexts, if spoken slowly and clearly.
